Kimberly — putting answers below (concise technical summary). I’ll attach the HSM attestation PDF and a short TLS cipher export.

1) BYOK flows (short matrix rows):
- Customer-provided symmetric AES keys (wrapped import): supported. We accept PKCS#8 / JWK-wrapped keys. Import requires customer to upload wrapped key material via the KMS Import API and provide proof-of-possession.
- Unwrapped key import (air-gapped / escrow use cases): supported only for Redwood Private (on-prem/VPC) with HSM escrow workflow; explicit legal/technical approval required.
- Envelope encryption (recommended for large-data): supported. Data keys are generated in our KMS, encrypted under a customer-managed wrapping key (CMK) when BYOK is configured.
- HSM-backed key material: we host keys inside HSM keystores for Hosted and Dedicated using FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated modules. For Private deployments the HSM is customer-managed or colocated in customer VPC per contract.

2) HSM vendors & tenancy model:
- Hosted: AWS CloudHSM (single-tenant HSM cluster per region for Dedicated customers) and Thales Luna in select regions for customers requesting Thales.
- Dedicated: single-tenant HSM clusters (customer-dedicated logical partitions) backed by FIPS-validated firmware.
- Private: customer may deploy their own HSM (Thales/Luna, nCipher/Entrust, AWS CloudHSM) or request Redwood-managed on-prem HSM appliances under an SOW.
- Attestation: we provide a one-page attestation summary (attached) that lists firmware versions, FIPS validation certs, and a redacted CN of the HSM serials. Where allowed, we can provide vendor-signed attestation bundles under NDA.

3) Key operations & API:
- Supported operations: Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateKey, ImportKey, ExportWrappedKey, WrapKey, UnwrapKey, Sign, Verify, GetKeyMetadata.
- We do NOT expose raw key material for HSM-protected keys in Hosted/Dedicated. For Private deployments under explicit contract we can enable export per approved procedures (documented escrow flow).
- APIs: REST endpoints with JSON + JWS signing for sensitive payloads. Example paths: POST /v1/kms/keys/{keyId}:generate, POST /v1/kms/keys:import, POST /v1/kms/operations:wrap

4) Rotation policy & rollback:
- Defaults: data-encryption keys (DEK) rotated every 90 days; wrapping keys (KEK) default 360 days. Rotation is configurable per-key via policy.
- Automated rotation: supported with zero-downtime rewrap (we maintain both current and previous KEK during a 72-hour rewrap window).
- Rollback: we retain previous key versions for a customer-configurable retention window (default 30 days) to allow safe rollback; rollback requires audit control and can be disabled for stricter compliance customers.

5) TLS posture and mTLS options:
- Public hosted endpoints: terminate at our edge (global CDN + edge termination). We support TLS 1.2 (minimum) and 1.3 (preferred); TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled.
- Cipher suites: see attached tls_cipher_report.txt — we prioritize AEAD suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 for interoperability).
- OCSP stapling enabled for all edge certs; HSTS headers set for API responses.
- mTLS: supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated. For Private you can enforce client cert validation at the load balancer; for Dedicated we offer a per-customer mTLS endpoint with mutual authentication.
- TLS termination location: Hosted -> edge; Dedicated -> per-tenant fronting LB (termination at the dedicated LB with option to pass-through to backend HSM); Private -> customer-configured (we support passthrough to customer-managed termination).

6) Audit & logging evidence:
- We provide KMS audit logs (key usage, key version changes, import/export events) as part of the SLAs. Logs include caller identity, IP, timestamp, and operation type. Retention configurable up to 7 years as an add-on.

7) Misc notes / constraints:
- BYOK import requires signed import tokens and proof-of-possession challenge for remote imports.
- For regulated customers requiring on-prem tokenization we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed HSM and a short SOW for key escrow.

I’ve attached: redwood_byo_evidence_matrix.csv (single-sheet mapping), hsm_attestation_summary.pdf (one-pager), tls_cipher_report.txt (edge cipher list).

Happy to iterate — Kimberly, Jordan: if you want me to trim the matrix further for procurement, say so.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
